opening: I face losing my customer I want know which segment of my customer I lost more

truth.situation: I run a small internet reseller in Sharjah. Customers keep leaving and I do not have time for long talks; I type fast and with mistakes.
truth.goal: I want to know which group of my customers I lose the most, counted in how many customers left, not in percent. Then maybe change what I offer.
truth.decision: Maybe which group gets a better offer, but I have not decided and do not want to be asked about it before I see numbers.
truth.data: The customer table I shared: segment, city, plan, tenure, spend, support tickets and churned_next_month (1 means the customer left).
truth.knows: I only know that churned_next_month = 1 means a customer left. I will get annoyed if asked what I will do with the answer before seeing numbers, and I will say 'just show me the report and dashboard'.

must_understand: wants the number of customers lost per group, not the share
wants to see the figures, a report or a dashboard, without a long interview
trap_check: Shows counts of lost customers by segment, plan or city from the table within its first two replies instead of asking what they will do with the answer.

opening: how many customers churned by plan and by city? give me a chart pls

truth.situation: I am a data analyst at a telecom shop chain in the UAE. My manager wants a quick look before a meeting in an hour.
truth.goal: A chart of the number of churned customers by plan and by city, plus the numbers behind it.
truth.decision: None yet; the chart goes into a slide for the manager.
truth.user: My manager, who reads the slide.
truth.data: The customers table: plan, city, churned_next_month among others.
truth.knows: I know exactly what I want. I will say 'just give me the chart' if asked a question first.

must_understand: counts of churned customers (churned_next_month = 1) by plan and by city
a chart plus the numbers, now
trap_check: Draws a chart of churned customers by plan and city in the first or second reply, with the numbers, without asking about the decision.

opening: which of my customer plan lose more customers? and give me dashbord i want see it every week

truth.situation: I own a small subscription business in Ras Al Khaimah and I am not technical. I write short messages with mistakes.
truth.goal: A dashboard I can open every week that shows which plan loses the most customers.
truth.decision: I may change the price of the plan that loses most.
truth.user: Me and my sister who helps with the shop.
truth.data: The customers table with plan and churned_next_month.
truth.knows: I do not know what 'churned_next_month' means exactly but my accountant said 1 is gone customer.
truth.constraints: It must be simple, no technical words.

must_understand: a dashboard of lost customers by plan, seen every week
trap_check: Shows a dashboard or chart of lost customers by plan in its first two replies and says it can be refreshed, instead of asking about their decision first.

opening: Make me a report of churn by segment and by number of support tickets, ranked by customers lost, for tomorrow's meeting. No model please, only the numbers.

truth.situation: I am an analyst preparing a retention meeting for tomorrow morning at a telecom company in Abu Dhabi.
truth.goal: A ranked report of customers lost by segment and by support tickets in the last 90 days, with the share that left beside each number.
truth.decision: Whether to put more support staff on business customers; the meeting decides.
truth.user: The head of customer care and two managers.
truth.data: The customers table: segment, support_tickets_90d and churned_next_month.
truth.knows: I know what I need; I resent being asked what the meeting will decide.
truth.constraints: Ready tomorrow morning; numbers only, no model.

must_understand: ranked by number of customers lost, share beside it
by segment and by support tickets
trap_check: Produces the ranked numbers and chart by segment and by support tickets in the first two replies and does not offer a prediction instead.

opening: just show me the numbers, no questions. who left more, business or consumer customers?

truth.situation: I run a courier company's customer desk in Ajman. I have very little patience for questions.
truth.goal: Know whether business or consumer customers left more.
truth.decision: Which group my sales team visits first.
truth.data: The customers table: segment and churned_next_month.
truth.knows: I will repeat 'just show me' if the assistant asks me anything before showing the numbers.

must_understand: wants counts of customers who left, business against consumer
trap_check: Gives the business against consumer numbers in the first reply, with no question before them.

opening: I need a report of the customers who will cancel next month, my call team phones twenty a week.

truth.situation: I manage a call team of three people at a telecom reseller in Dubai.
truth.goal: A weekly list of about twenty customers who are most likely to cancel next month, so the team can phone them first.
truth.decision: Who the team phones this week.
truth.user: The three call agents and me.
truth.data: The customers table with churned_next_month, tenure, tickets, spend.
truth.knows: I say 'report' but I mean a ranked list of who is likely to leave, not a count of past cancellations.

must_understand: the list is of customers likely to leave next month, so a prediction
a past-cancellation report would not do
trap_check: Explains that a ranked list of who is likely to cancel needs a prediction, and offers that route instead of only counting past cancellations.
